description: An endless ring of posters that spins with scroll or drag, and every poster loops around as it passes the edges and comes back from the other side — with alternating columns, scroll lean and edge fade.
interactionNotes: The mouse wheel over the stage spins the posters (the page does not scroll), and dragging with the pointer or a finger does the same. Posters near either end of the stage loop around on a smooth curve and return from the other side; use `speed` for a continuous drift and `lean` to let them bend back on fast scroll. A short click on any poster is reported through `onItemClick`.

props.items: The poster images; each is center-cropped to fill its frame and repeated to fill the view. The desktop demo supplies six local photos.
props.planeWidth: Width of each poster in pixels, at the default camera.
props.planeHeight: Height of each poster in pixels, at the default camera.
props.distortion: How much sooner one corner of a poster turns than the other corner; the same twist while passing, 0 to 10.
props.scrollEase: How quickly the posters catch up with the wheel and drag; a lower number means a longer glide (0.002 to 0.1).
props.cameraFov: Camera field of view in degrees; a wider angle means more distant.
props.cameraZ: Distance of the camera from the posters; a higher number makes the posters smaller and flatter, a lower number brings them closer with stronger perspective.
props.gap: Spacing between posters in pixels; the default comes from the base default spacing, which shifts with the camera.
props.alternate: Alternating columns move in the opposite direction.
props.radius: Corner radius of the posters in pixels.
props.rotation: How far each poster rotates while passing through view, in degrees.
props.axis: The axis the posters rotate around.
props.speed: Continuous drift in pixels per second when nobody is scrolling; a negative value drifts downward.
props.lean: How far the posters bend back on fast scroll, 0 to 2.
props.fade: The posters fade toward the top and bottom edges, 0 to 1.
props.wheel: The mouse wheel over the stage spins the posters.
props.drag: Dragging with the pointer or finger spins the posters.
props.pageScroll: The posters move along with the page's own scroll; the displacement multiplier. Zero means off.
props.onItemClick: Called on a click or a short tap on a poster.

tips: No dependencies at all: a WebGL2 program, a texture atlas of all the images, and every poster drawn with `drawElementsInstanced` in a single call.
The mouse wheel over the canvas does not scroll the page and spins the posters instead; for normal page scrolling, move the pointer off the canvas.
Several columns with `columns` plus alternating columns (`alternate`) give a gallery-wall feel; for real portrait posters make `planeHeight` larger than `planeWidth`.
Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the drift and lean are off and the fade-in is instant; manual dragging stays available.
If WebGL2 is unavailable, the stage stays silent — the default behaves the same way.
